subject: Biotechnology
title: Quality Control in Biologics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Quality Control in Biologics usable.

hook.text: A single misfolded protein can kill — quality control in biologic manufacturing is a matter of life and death.

buildup.text: Mass spectrometry confirms the protein's exact mass and amino acid sequence — every batch is verified.

discovery.text: Glycan profiling ensures sugar modifications are consistent — even small changes affect drug safety and efficacy.

twist.text: Aggregation is the silent killer — clumped proteins trigger immune reactions. Size exclusion catches aggregates.

climax.text: Process analytical technology monitors quality in real time — catching problems during production, not after.

punchline.text: Test everything, trust nothing — QC keeps biologics safe.

quiz.question: Why is protein aggregation a safety concern in biologics?
options: Aggregated proteins are always inactive and waste money
Clumped proteins can trigger dangerous immune reactions in patients
Aggregation makes proteins too large to inject
